fullPassage:
Choosing a career is one of the biggest life decisions young people face. Mapping out the right career path can be demanding. While some teenagers have a clear vision of their career goals, others struggle to define them. This is where role models can be useful. They help young people start to plan their careers by providing them with guidance and the sense of purpose they need to succeed. We asked our teenage readers about their role models and the qualities they admire most in them. After you read each student's story, you will get a better idea of the profound impact role models can have when it comes to shaping career goals.

My role model is Jacques Cousteau, a French ocean explorer, inventor, and filmmaker. He dedicated his life to exploring and documenting the wonders of the underwater world. As a young man, he dreamed of becoming a pilot, but then he broke both of his arms in a terrible car accident. As part of his physical therapy, Cousteau began swimming. He became intrigued by the mysteries of the ocean, and he wanted to explore further. However, the diving equipment available at that time was insufficient. Instead of giving up, Cousteau decided to create his own equipment. After a long series of failed attempts, he finally succeeded in developing a portable breathing device, which he called the "Aqua-Lung." Cousteau shared his underwater experiences with the world in a compelling documentary film released in 1956. It transformed people's perceptions of the ocean and promoted the need for marine conservation.

Cousteau's curiosity drove him to constantly challenge himself in new areas, and his passion enabled him to make the impossible a reality. Cousteau's life story inspired me to push the boundaries of what I can do. Because of him, I am not afraid to try different things in life. I will keep exploring until I find what suits me best.

When people ask me about my role model, I always say that it is Joan Procter. You may not have heard of her, but she was a notable zoologist who specialized in reptiles in the early 20th century. She taught me that devotion to a particular field is important for shaping one's career. During her childhood, Procter immersed herself in the exploration of nature and animals. Although her father hated reptiles, she kept lizards, snakes, and even a baby crocodile as pets. They were special companions that she loved and took care of. She was a brilliant student, but health problems prevented her from attending university. However, her passion for zoology was so strong that it kept her moving forward, and she continued her studies on her own.

Procter accumulated extensive knowledge of zoology. She began exchanging letters with George Boulenger, a prominent expert on reptiles, in order to share ideas. He was so impressed that he hired her as his assistant at the British Museum. A few years later, she became the first female curator of reptiles at the London Zoo. There, she actively contributed to the design of the Reptile House by incorporating new technology that allowed for better care and breeding of wild animals. Like her, I want to dedicate myself to a field that I have a passion for. For this reason, I will take my time to think deeply about where my true interests lie. If I am fortunate, one of my passions might someday lead to a rewarding career.

As someone who loves animation, my role model has always been Kim Sang-jin. He was the first Korean animator to work for Walt Disney Animation Studios. Beyond the fact that he worked for a world-famous company, I admire him for pursuing his dream despite the difficulties he faced. From a young age, Kim was enthusiastic about drawing. However, his dream of studying art in college was disrupted when he was diagnosed with color vision deficiency during high school. Surprisingly, he didn't allow this misfortune to discourage him. Instead, he simply viewed his condition as a minor issue that could happen to anyone.

Although he graduated with a degree in economics, he searched for a job related to art that wouldn't involve working with colors. He found out that some animators work only in pencil, so he sent his portfolio to all the animation studios in Korea. One of them gave him an opportunity, and he was finally able to start his career. It was his hard work and talent that eventually led him to a position at Disney at the age of 37. I give him a lot of credit for his persistence and his attitude toward the challenges in his life. I'll never give up on my dreams. If I encounter difficulties, I will simply find another way to pursue them, just as he did.

These stories shared by our readers emphasize the importance of role models in guiding teenagers toward their career goals. Role models, regardless of their field, inspire us because they possess qualities like persistence, commitment, and optimism. If you haven't found a role model yet, perhaps it's time to start searching for one. Try to find someone who can encourage you to take the first step in your career exploration.

questions.passage: Choosing a career is one of the biggest life decisions young people face. Mapping out the right career path can be ①<u>demanding</u>. While some teenagers have a clear vision of their career goals, others struggle ②<u>to define</u> them. This is where role models can be useful. They help young people start to plan their careers by ③<u>providing</u> them with guidance and the sense of purpose they need ④<u>succeed</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'they need to succeed'인데, 'to'가 빠져서 어법상 틀림.
det.analysis:
✅ ① demanding: be동사 뒤 형용사 보어 정상
✅ ② to define: struggle + to부정사 정상
✅ ③ providing: by + 동명사 정상
❌ ④ succeed → to succeed: need + to부정사 구문에서 to 필요
det.tip: need + to부정사: ~할 필요가 있다. by + ~ing: ~함으로써. struggle + to부정사: ~하려고 애쓰다.

questions.passage: My role model is Jacques Cousteau, a French ocean explorer, inventor, and filmmaker. He dedicated his life to ①<u>exploring</u> and documenting the wonders of the underwater world. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 'dreamed of becoming'인데, 'become'으로 바뀌어 틀림. 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사(-ing)가 와야 함.
det.analysis:
✅ ① exploring: dedicate ~ to(전치사) + 동명사 정상
❌ ② become → becoming: dream of + 동명사. of는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사 필요
✅ ③ began: begin + 동명사(swimming) 과거시제 정상
✅ ④ to explore: want + to부정사 정상
det.tip: 전치사 + 동명사: of ~ing, by ~ing, in ~ing, for ~ing. 전치사 뒤에 동사원형은 올 수 없다.

questions.passage: She taught me that devotion to a particular field is important for ①<u>shaping</u> one's career. During her childhood, Procter immersed ②<u>herself</u> in the exploration of nature and animals. Although her father hated reptiles, she kept lizards, snakes, and even a baby crocodile as pets. They were special companions ③<u>that</u> she loved and took care of. She was a brilliant student, but health problems prevented her ④<u>to attend</u> university.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'prevented her from attending'인데, 'to attend'로 바뀌어 틀림.
det.analysis:
✅ ① shaping: for(전치사) + 동명사 정상
✅ ② herself: immerse oneself in 재귀대명사 정상
✅ ③ that: 관계대명사 목적격, 선행사 companions 정상
❌ ④ to attend → from attending: prevent + O + from ~ing 구문
det.tip: prevent/stop/keep + 목적어 + from ~ing: ~가 …하는 것을 막다.

questions.passage: Although he graduated with a degree in economics, he searched for a job ①<u>related</u> to art that wouldn't involve working with colors. He found out that some animators work only in pencil, so he sent his portfolio to all the animation studios in Korea. One of them gave him an opportunity, and he was finally able to start his career. It was his hard work and talent ②<u>what</u> eventually led him to a position at Disney at the age of 37. I give him a lot of credit for his persistence and his attitude ③<u>toward</u> the challenges in his life. If I ④<u>encounter</u> difficulties, I will simply find another way to pursue them.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 'It was ~ that eventually led him'인데, 'what'으로 바뀌어 틀림. 강조구문 'It is/was ~ that …'에서 that이 필수.
det.analysis:
✅ ① related: 과거분사 — a job related to art 명사 수식 정상
❌ ② what → that: It was ~ that … 강조구문에서 that 필수. what은 선행사 포함 관계대명사로 이 구문에 불가
✅ ③ toward: 전치사 — attitude toward ~ 정상
✅ ④ encounter: 조건절(If I encounter) 현재시제 정상
det.tip: 강조구문: It is/was + 강조 대상 + that + 나머지. what은 강조구문에 쓸 수 없다.

questions.passage: Cousteau's curiosity drove him to constantly challenge himself in new areas, and his passion enabled him to make the impossible a reality. Cousteau's life story ①<u>inspired</u> me to push the boundaries of what I can do. Because of him, I am not ②<u>afraid</u> to try different things in life. I will keep ③<u>hesitating</u> until I find what suits me best. These stories shared by our readers ④<u>emphasize</u> the importance of role models.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'keep exploring(탐구하다)'인데, 'hesitating(망설이다)'로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① inspired(영감을 주다): 원문 일치
✅ ② afraid(두려운): 원문 일치
❌ ③ hesitating(망설이다) → exploring(탐구하다): '두렵지 않다'는 앞 문맥과 '망설인다'는 모순
✅ ④ emphasize(강조하다): 원문 일치
det.tip: exploring(탐구하다) ↔ hesitating(망설이다). 'not afraid' + 'keep exploring'이 자연스러운 흐름.

questions.passage: She began exchanging letters with George Boulenger, a prominent expert on reptiles, in order to share ideas. He was so ①<u>impressed</u> that he hired her as his assistant at the British Museum. A few years later, she became the first female ②<u>curator</u> of reptiles at the London Zoo. There, she actively contributed to the design of the Reptile House by ③<u>eliminating</u> new technology that allowed for better care and breeding of wild animals. Like her, I want to ④<u>dedicate</u> myself to a field that I have a passion for.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'incorporating(포함시키다)'인데, 'eliminating(제거하다)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① impressed(감명받은): 원문 일치
✅ ② curator(큐레이터): 원문 일치
❌ ③ eliminating(제거하다) → incorporating(포함시키다): '더 잘 돌볼 수 있게 하는 새 기술'을 제거하는 것은 비논리적
✅ ④ dedicate(헌신하다): 원문 일치
det.tip: incorporating(포함시키다) ↔ eliminating(제거하다). 'better care and breeding'이 단서.

questions.passage: My role model is Jacques Cousteau, a French ocean explorer, inventor, and filmmaker. He dedicated his life to exploring and documenting the wonders of the underwater world. questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Cousteau는 젊었을 때 조종사가 되기를 꿈꿨다."

det.korean: 원문: 'he dreamed of becoming a pilot' → T(일치)

det.korean: 원문: 'her father hated reptiles' → 아버지는 싫어했고, 키운 것은 Procter 자신. F(불일치)
det.analysis: ❌ F: '좋아했다'가 아니라 '싫어했다(hated)'. 함께 키운 것이 아니라 Procter 혼자 키움.

"김상진은 27세에 Disney에서 일하게 되었다."

det.korean: 원문: 'at the age of 37' → 37세이지 27세가 아니다. F(불일치)
det.analysis: ❌ F: 숫자 변조 — 37세를 27세로 바꿈
det.tip: 내용일치 문제에서 숫자(나이, 년도)는 자주 변조되는 포인트.

questions.passage: He became intrigued by the mysteries of the ocean, and he wanted to explore further. However, the diving equipment available at that time was insufficient. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 오랜 실패한 시도들(failed attempts) 끝에 마침내 성공했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ failed attempts: 'finally succeeded'가 단서 — 최종적으로 성공은 이전 실패를 암시
❌ ① successes: 성공 뒤에 또 성공이면 'finally'가 불필요
❌ ② careful plans: 'a long series of'와 어울리지 않음
❌ ③ funded projects: 문맥에 자금 지원 언급 없음
det.tip: a long series of failed attempts: 오랜 일련의 실패. finally(마침내)가 핵심 단서.

questions.passage: Procter accumulated extensive knowledge of zoology. She began exchanging letters with George Boulenger, a prominent expert on reptiles, in order to share ideas. He was so impressed that he hired her as his assistant at the British Museum. A few years later, she became the first female curator of reptiles at the London Zoo. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: better care and breeding of wild animals

reducing the number of reptile species

det.korean: 새 기술을 포함시켜 야생 동물을 더 잘 돌보고 번식시킬 수 있게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① better care and breeding of wild animals: 원문 일치. 동물학자이자 큐레이터로서 동물 복지가 핵심
❌ ② 관광객 유치는 동물학자의 주된 관심사가 아님
❌ ③ 종 수를 줄이는 것은 큐레이터 목적과 반대
❌ ④ 화석/유물은 박물관이지 동물원 맥락이 아님
det.tip: Reptile House = 파충류관. 큐레이터로서 동물 복지 향상이 핵심 목적.

questions.passage: As someone who loves animation, my role model has always been Kim Sang-jin. He was the first Korean animator to work for Walt Disney Animation Studios. Beyond the fact that he worked for a world-famous company, I admire him for pursuing his dream despite the difficulties he faced. From a young age, Kim was enthusiastic about drawing. However, his dream of studying art in college was disrupted when he was diagnosed with color vision deficiency during high school.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 김상진은 초등학교 때 색약 진단을 받았다.
김상진은 두 번째로 Disney에서 일한 한국인이었다.
김상진은 어렸을 때부터 그림 그리기에 열정적이었다.

det.korean: ④ 원문: 'From a young age, Kim was enthusiastic about drawing.'
det.analysis:
❌ ① 미술 전공 아님 — 색약으로 꿈 좌절, 경제학 졸업
❌ ② 초등학교가 아니라 '고등학교(high school)' 때 진단
❌ ③ '두 번째'가 아니라 '최초의(the first)' 한국인
✅ ④ 'enthusiastic about drawing'과 일치
det.tip: 시기(초등학교/고등학교), 순서(최초/두 번째), 전공을 세밀하게 비교.

questions.passage: Procter accumulated extensive knowledge of zoology. She began exchanging letters with George Boulenger, a prominent expert on reptiles, in order to share ideas. He was so impressed that he hired her as his assistant at the British Museum. A few years later, she became the first female curator of reptiles at the London Zoo. There, she actively contributed to the design of the Reptile House by incorporating new technology.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Procter는 동물학에 대해 광범위한 지식을 쌓았다.
Boulenger는 Procter를 British Museum에서 조수로 채용했다.
Procter는 Boulenger의 추천으로 London Zoo에 바로 취직했다.
Procter는 Reptile House의 설계에 적극적으로 기여했다.

det.korean: ③ 원문: 'A few years later(몇 년 후)' → '바로 취직'이 아님. 또한 '추천'이 아니라 British Museum 조수로 먼저 채용.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'accumulated extensive knowledge'와 일치
✅ ② 'hired her as his assistant at the British Museum'과 일치
❌ ③ '몇 년 후'인데 '바로'로 변조, '추천'도 사실과 다름
✅ ④ 'actively contributed to the design'과 일치
det.tip: 'A few years later' ≠ '바로'. 시간 표현 변조 주의.

questions.passage: ① Cousteau shared his underwater experiences with the world in a compelling documentary film releasing in 1956. ② It transformed people's perceptions of the ocean and promoted the need for marine conservation. ③ Cousteau's curiosity drove him to constantly challenge himself in new areas. ④ His passion enabled him to make the impossible a reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 ①~④ 중에서 문법적 오류가 있는 문장은?

det.korean: ① 원문은 'a compelling documentary film released in 1956'인데, 'releasing'으로 바뀌어 틀림. 과거분사(released)가 맞다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① releasing → released: 다큐멘터리 영화가 '개봉된' 것이므로 수동(과거분사). releasing은 능동으로 어색
✅ ② 문법 정상
✅ ③ drove him to constantly challenge — 분리부정사 허용
✅ ④ enabled him to make — enable + O + to부정사 정상
det.tip: 현재분사 vs 과거분사: releasing(개봉하는 — 능동) vs released(개봉된 — 수동). film은 개봉되는 대상이므로 과거분사 released.

questions.passage: She taught me that devotion to a particular field is important for shaping one's career. During her childhood, Procter immersed herself in the exploration of nature and animals. Although her father hated reptiles, she kept lizards, snakes, and even a baby crocodile as pets. They were special companions that she loved and took care of.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"Procter는 어린 시절 자연과 동물 탐험에 __________ 했다."

det.korean: Procter는 어린 시절 자연과 동물 탐험에 몰두했다(immersed).
det.analysis: ✅ immersed: 'Procter immersed herself in the exploration of nature and animals'에서 찾을 수 있음
det.tip: immerse oneself in ~: ~에 몰두하다. 패러프레이징: '탐험에 몰두했다' = 'immersed herself in the exploration'

questions.passage: Cousteau's curiosity drove him to constantly challenge himself in new areas. Cousteau's life story inspired me to push the __________ (boundary) of what I can do.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 내가 할 수 있는 것의 한계들(boundaries)을 뛰어넘도록 영감을 주었다.
det.analysis: ✅ boundaries: push the boundaries of ~는 관용 표현으로 항상 복수형
det.tip: boundary → boundaries: -y → -ies. push the boundaries = 한계를 넓히다(관용 표현, 항상 복수)

questions.passage: However, the diving equipment available at that time was insufficient. Instead of giving up, Cousteau decided to create his own equipment. After a long series of failed attempts, __________. Cousteau shared his underwater experiences with the world in a compelling documentary film released in 1956.
questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오.

[he / finally / succeeded / in / developing / a / portable / breathing / device]

questions.passage: These stories shared by our readers emphasize the importance of role models in guiding teenagers toward their career goals. Role models, regardless of their field, inspire us because they possess qualities like persistence, commitment, and optimism. If you haven't found a role model yet, perhaps it's time to start searching for one. Try to find someone who can encourage you to take the first step in your career exploration.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글의 주제: 진로 탐색에서 롤모델의 중요성
det.analysis:
✅ ② 'importance of role models in guiding teenagers toward career goals'와 직접 대응
❌ ① 부모 역할 언급 없음

det.tip: 'emphasize the importance of role models'가 주제문.

questions.passage: When people ask me about my role model, I always say that it is Joan Procter. You may not have heard of her, but she was a notable zoologist who specialized in reptiles in the early 20th century. She taught me that devotion to a particular field is important for shaping one's career. During her childhood, Procter immersed herself in the exploration of nature and animals. Although her father hated reptiles, she kept lizards, snakes, and even a baby crocodile as pets. She was a brilliant student, but health problems prevented her from attending university. However, her passion for zoology was so strong that it kept her moving forward, and she continued her studies on her own.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 대학 교육 없이는 전문가가 되기 어렵다.
특정 분야에 대한 헌신이 진로 형성에 중요하다.
부모의 반대를 이겨내는 것이 성공의 핵심이다.

det.korean: 요지: 특정 분야에 대한 헌신이 진로 형성에 중요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 'devotion to a particular field is important for shaping one's career' 직접 패러프레이징
❌ ① 건강 문제는 장애물이었지 핵심 주장 아님
❌ ② 대학 못 갔지만 성공 → 이 주장과 반대
❌ ④ 아버지 반대는 배경 정보일 뿐
det.tip: 'She taught me that ~'가 화자가 배운 교훈 = 글의 요지.
